title: Lombardy Poplar: Old Lombardy Poplars You Can Visit
meta_description: A columnar poplar bred to be thin and short-lived. Three mapped, one in Portland with the widest trunk on the city's entire heritage register.
intro: Lombardy poplar is the columnar form of black poplar, propagated only from cuttings of a single line, so every one traces back to the same origin tree and none of them set seed. It is also famously short-lived: usually rotten by fifty, gone by seventy, planted by the million and protected almost nowhere. The three mapped here are the exceptions. Amsterdam's stands as a living pilaster in the Rijksmuseum's garden of salvaged doorways, planted within a few decades of the museum's 1885 opening. Seattle's grew up beside the temporary Fine Arts Palace built for the 1909 Alaska-Yukon-Pacific Exposition and has now outlasted the building it was planted to frame. Portland's, out on the eastern edge of the city, carries the widest trunk on the entire heritage tree register at 9.75 metres round, an absurd measurement for a tree built to be thin.
